info.name: LegiScore Partner API: reference
info.description:
Generated by spec/build_postman.py from legiscore-openapi.json. Do not edit by hand.

Every operation the partner API exposes, grouped by module. For the order you actually integrate in, use the guided collection beside this one.

Programmatic access to LegiScore legal opinion reports and government record searches.

Authentication: send your `lsk_` key as `X-API-Key` (or `Authorization: Bearer lsk_...`).
Rate limits are per key. Exceeding one returns 429 with a `Retry-After` header.

Reports: presign + upload documents, POST /api/requests to create the case, then either poll `/api/cases/{case_id}/status` or receive a webhook. A case can pause for missing documents, document review, or risk acknowledgements; each pause has a matching resume endpoint.

Search is a separate product: its own credit balance, its own host (named as a `servers` entry on each search path), and a flat per-search price that the catalog endpoint states. Submit a search, then poll it until its status is `succeeded`, `failed` or `cancelled`.

variable.description: A translation session id from POST /api/v1/translate/submit.
The position of a slot in the missing-documents list, starting at 0.
The id of one of your registered webhooks.

item.name: core
item.description: Uploads, credit balance and scenario reference data. Shared by every module.

request.description: List the diligence scenarios your key may run, optionally filtered by category or state. A scenario is the template a case runs against: it decides which searches run, which fields are extracted and which template the report uses. Scenarios published for everyone and scenarios configured for your organisation both appear.
Return the credit balances your key can draw on, and which one a new case would be charged to by default. The key itself determines the organisation; there is no account or tenant identifier to pass.
List the custom field schemas your key may attach to a new case through custom_field_schema_ids. The set is resolved from your key: your own, your organisation's, and any published for general use.

Confirm that the PUT finished and register the file, using the objectName that presignUpload returned. Returns the document_id you pass to createCase. Call it only after the PUT has returned 200; calling it early is rejected. An Idempotency-Key header is honoured, so a retried call after a lost response returns the first result instead of registering the file twice.

Ask for a short-lived signed URL to upload one file straight to object storage. Send the file name, its byte size and its content type; you get back the URL to PUT the bytes to and an objectName to pass to completeUpload once the PUT returns 200. The content type must be one we accept and the size must be within the per-file limit, both of which are checked here rather than on the PUT.

item.name: reports
item.description: Create a legal opinion case, follow it to completion, answer review pauses, fetch the report.

request.description: Read the title risks a case has raised, together with any decisions already recorded. Valid only while the case is paused at the acknowledgement checkpoint.

Resume a case paused for missing documents, either by supplying new document ids or by setting proceed_anyway so the report is produced and records the gap. Answering one pause can surface the next, so poll the status again afterwards rather than assuming the case is finished. Two replies mean the case did not move: 422 with a PAUSE_GATE_UNMET code, which lists what your organisation still needs actioned and is refused again on a retry of the same body, and a 200 carrying pending_checker, which records your answer and holds the case at this pause until a second person approves it.

Read the details extracted from your documents before the government-record searches run against them: document number, date, parties, survey number, house number. Valid only while the case is paused at the document-analysis checkpoint.

Inventory every file a case produced: the documents you uploaded, anything added during a review pause, the search artefacts and the report itself. Each entry carries a short-lived signed download URL, so fetch what you need soon after listing rather than storing the URLs.

item.name: Download all case files as a ZIP

request.description: Stream every file on the case as a single ZIP, foldered by kind, optionally narrowed with the kinds filter. The response is binary, not JSON. Very large archives are refused rather than truncated.

Read the documents a case is waiting for. Valid only while the case is paused at the missing-documents checkpoint; asking at any other time returns 400 rather than an empty list, so dispatch on internal_status from getCaseStatus first.

item.name: Link documents to a missing-documents slot

request.description: Attach documents you have uploaded to one specific slot in the missing-documents list, so the case shows which requested document each upload satisfies. Optional: continueCase accepts the same document ids without slot detail. This one endpoint needs an extra permission on your key; a 403 here means asking us to grant it, not a bad request.

Return the completed report and property score for a case. While the case is still running this returns 409 with the current state rather than a partial report, so poll getCaseStatus and call this once the state is completed.

Poll a case. Returns a stable public state (queued, running, awaiting_review, completed, failed), a progress figure, a human-readable message and your own metadata echoed back. Built to be called often; every ten seconds is a sensible floor.

Record a decision against each risk and release the case for final report generation. This writes a legal acceptance record attributed to whoever's key made the call, so it should carry a person's decision rather than a default set in code. Send each item back whole with a decision added; dropping fields off the generated item loses information the report needs. Two replies mean the case did not move: 422 with a PAUSE_GATE_UNMET code, which lists the risks still undecided or still missing the comment your organisation requires, and a 200 carrying pending_checker, which holds the case here until a second person approves your answer.

Accept the extracted details as they are, or send corrections as a list of field updates, then let the searches run. A wrong survey number here makes every downstream search wrong, so this is the cheapest place to fix one. Two replies mean the case did not move: 422 with a PAUSE_GATE_UNMET code, which lists the findings your organisation still needs marked as seen, and a 200 carrying pending_checker, which holds the case here until a second person approves your answer. Findings are marked as seen in the web application; a case whose organisation requires that is refused until someone does.

Open a new case over documents you have already uploaded. Requires documentIds and a propertyFocus object describing the property; every other field has a default resolved from your key. Each document id is checked to be yours before anything is charged. Returns the case_id you use for every later call. Supply an Idempotency-Key header and a repeat of the same request returns the first response rather than opening and charging a second case; the same key with a different body is rejected.
Download the report for a case in the requested format. Ownership is enforced against your key: another organisation's case is reported as not found rather than as forbidden.

item.name: search
item.description: Run a government record search and collect what the portal returns. Its own credit balance, and its own host.

request.description: Run one government record search, or up to 25 in one call. Send state, search_type and the params that pair needs, or a searches array of the same fields with an optional label per item. Returns 202 with the accepted searches, each carrying the id you poll, plus rejected for any item that failed validation, credits_charged for the run and a batch_id when more than one search was accepted. A batch runs the items that validated rather than failing as a whole. Search credits are a separate balance from the report credits getCredits returns: they are priced flat per search at the rate getSearchCatalog states, charged when a search is accepted, and returned if the source cannot be reached. Too few of them returns 402 with the code insufficient_credits. An identical search already run on your account within the last 24 hours is answered from that result instead of the source, and replayed counts how many were.

List the searches on your account, newest first, with limit and offset paging and optional filters on status and batch_id. Each entry is the same shape getSearch returns, and anything still in flight is refreshed on the way past, so listing doubles as polling. Returns the page plus the total count.

item.name: Propose search parameters from a document

request.description: Read a document and propose the parameters for a search, without running one. Send multipart/form-data with a file (PDF, PNG, JPEG or WebP, under 20 MB) or a text field, plus the state. Returns the extracted fields, each with a confidence, and needs_review when any of them is low. It deliberately never submits: a wrong survey number does not fail loudly, it searches a different property and returns a confident, wrong result, so a person confirms first. Priced separately at the rate getSearchCatalog states, and a document nothing could be read from costs nothing.

Return everything that can be searched: the states that are live, every search type within them, the fields each one takes and which are required, what a result yields, how long it usually takes and the current price per search. It also reports whether the government source is reachable right now. This call needs no key, so it is the reference you build a search form or a parameter mapping from before you have one.

Return your search credit balance, how much of it is currently spendable, whether it is personal or your organisation's, the current prices and the most recent movements against it. This balance is separate from the report credits getCredits returns, so a run of searches can never spend the credits bought to produce legal opinion reports.

item.name: Resolve a lookup to its codes

request.description: Resolve names to the codes a search parameter needs, one dimension at a time: districts, mandals, villages, sub-registrar offices and the rest. Pass dim, plus the district or mandal already chosen where the dimension is nested, and q to narrow by name. Returns the matching options, each with the codes to send in params. getSearchCatalog names the dimension every lookup field uses.

Poll one search. Returns its status (queued, running, awaiting_otp, succeeded, failed or cancelled), a progress figure, and once it settles the found verdict, the extracted records and the documents the source issued. A succeeded search with found false means the source was reached and had nothing on record against the property, which is a result rather than a failure. credits_charged and refunded say what this search actually cost.

Ask a search that is still in flight to stop. Returns the search as it stands, with cancelling true; the settled status arrives on a later poll, and the credits are returned if it never completed. A search that has already succeeded, failed or been cancelled returns 409 rather than being cancelled twice.

item.name: Download a document from a search

request.description: Download one of the files a search produced, named by the filename getSearch reports under documents. The API answers with a redirect to a signed URL that expires in an hour; the SDK follows it for you on a connection that carries no API key, and hands you the bytes. The response is binary, not JSON. The file is looked up in the search's own document list rather than from the path, so a filename that is not on this search is reported as not found, and one that belongs to another account is reported the same way.

Hand a one-time password to a search whose status is awaiting_otp, as 4 to 8 digits in otp. Returns accepted true once it has been passed on. A search in any other status returns 409. Most searches never reach this state; it exists for the case where the source sends its code to a number you hold.

Re-run a finished search against related identifiers, for when the first attempt came back with less than expected. Takes no body: it reads what did come back and works out what else is worth asking. Returns 202 with the additional searches it started and the reasoning behind them. Priced separately from a plain search, at the rate getSearchCatalog states, and nothing is charged when the source is unreachable or when the analysis finds nothing defensible to try. Only a search that has succeeded or failed can be recovered, and a recovery run cannot itself be recovered.

item.name: translate
item.description: Translate a document into another Indian language.

request.description: Translate a DOCX file and return the translated DOCX directly in the response. Synchronous, for documents small enough to wait on; use submitTranslation for anything larger.
List the language codes translation accepts as a target.
Return a short-lived signed URL for the translated document. Fetch it promptly rather than storing the URL.
List your translation sessions, newest first, with limit and offset paging.
Poll a translation session. Returns pages completed against pages total, the session state and any error message.
Upload a PDF for asynchronous translation and return a session id. Credits are deducted per page at submission. Poll getTranslationStatus, then downloadTranslation once it reports complete.

item.name: extraction
item.description: Pull structured property details out of an uploaded document.

request.description: Upload one or more documents and get back a job id for asynchronous extraction of the property details they describe. Poll getPropertyExtraction for the result. Optionally pass a search schema so the result also carries values shaped ready to feed into a raw search.
Poll a property extraction job. Returns its current state, the extracted result once it is done, or the error if it failed.

item.name: webhooks
item.description: Manage your own delivery endpoints: list, create, update, delete, rotate secret.

request.description: List the delivery endpoints registered against your key, with their events and whether each is active. Secrets are never returned here.

Register a delivery endpoint and the events it should receive. The signing secret is returned exactly once, in this response, and can never be read back: store it as you receive it. Deliveries are signed with it, and your handler should verify every one.
Change the name, URL, event list, custom headers or active flag of one of your webhooks. Fields you omit are left as they are. Changing the URL does not change the signing secret.
Remove one of your webhooks. Deliveries stop immediately and the signing secret is gone with it.
Issue a new signing secret for one of your webhooks. The new secret is returned exactly once and the old one stops verifying at once, so deploy the new secret to your handler in the same change.
